name: The Class for Representing a Loan (Case 1)
description:
Construct a class that represents a loan. This class should contain data representing the interest rate, loan amount, and the length of loan period (in years). The class should have constructors that permits a loan to be created when:
 - annual interest rate, length of loan period, and loan amount are specified
 - none of the properties of the loan are specified. In this, we create a loan with default values for the loan properties (3 % interest rate, 1-year loan period, and 1000 loan amount).
The other method of the this class should calculate the amount of monthly payments on the loan.

The LoanTester1 class instantiates an object from this class and invokes its method to determine the amount of monthly payments on the loan.

comments.content: We define the class LoanTester1 to demonstrate the creation and use of Loan1 objects.
We need to read and process the value that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the annual interest rate for the loan.
We need to read the annual interest rate for the loan and store it in a variable. We read the input by calling the nextDouble() method because this input could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.
We prompt the user to enter the number of years for the loan period.
We need to read the number of years for the loan period and store it in a variable. We read the input by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We prompt the user to enter the loan amount.
We need to read the loan amount and store it in a variable. We read the input by calling the nextDouble() method because this input could have a decimal point.
Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid double value.

This statement creates a Loan1 object with the specified annual interest rate, number of years for the loan period, and loan amount. Note that we create this object by using the new keyword and writing its initial values in parentheses (annual interest rate, number of years, loan amount). The variable loan holds a reference to a Loan1 object.

Note that we can create a Loan1  object with the specified annual interest rate, number of years for the loan period, and loan amount only when we have a constructor in the Loan1 class that accepts these parameters in the order that they are specified.
We want to use the currency formatting for the monthly payments. Therefore, we request an object from getCurrencyInstance() method.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the monthly payments on the loan. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

Note that we get the amount of monthly payments by invoking the method getMonthlyPayment of loan.

The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and the formatted value returned by invoking the getMonthlyPayment method of the loan object.

Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned value from this method in a variable. We could use the returned value directly in the println statement.
We define the class Loan1 to represent a loan with a service for calculating monthly payments

Every object of the Loan1 class will have its own annual interest rate. Therefore, we need to declare an instance variable for the class to store the interest for the loan. We declare it as double because the interest rate has a decimal point.
Note that an instance variable is a variable defined in a class, for which each instantiated object of the class has a separate copy, or instance.

Although, instance variable annualInterestRate has not been initialized, it has the default value of 0.0. Because, unlike local variables, which are not automatically initialized, every instance variable has a default initial value. The default value for an instance variable of type double is 0.0.

The instance variables should be declared as private to restrict the direct access or change from outside the class. In this way, no unexpected modification of the object data is possible.
We could access/change the private instance variables of the class only through the getters/setters methods of the class.

Every object of the Loan1 class will have its own loan periods. Therefore, we need to declare an instance variable for the class to store the length of the loan periods. We declare this variable as int because the length of loan periods (number of years) is an integer.
Note that an instance variable is a variable defined in a class, for which each instantiated object of the class has a separate copy, or instance.

Although, instance variable numberOfYears has not been initialized, it has the default value of 0. Because, unlike local variables, which are not automatically initialized, every instance variable has a default initial value. The default value for an instance variable of type int is 0.

The instance variables should be declared as private to restrict the direct access or change from outside the class. In this way, no unexpected modification of the object data is possible.
We could access/change the private instance variables of the class only through the getters/setters methods of the class.

Every object of the Loan1 class will have its own loan amount. Therefore, we need to declare an instance variable for the class to store the loan amount. We declare this variable as double because the loan amount could have a decimal point.
Note that an instance variable is a variable defined in a class, for which each instantiated object of the class has a separate copy, or instance.

Although, instance variable loanAmount has not been initialized, it has the default value of 0.0. Because, unlike local variables, which are not automatically initialized, every instance variable has a default initial value. The default value for an instance variable of type double is 0.0.

The instance variables should be declared as private to restrict the direct access or change from outside the class. In this way, no unexpected modification of the object data is possible.
We could access/change the private instance variables of the class only through the getters/setters methods of the class.

To specify the initial values for the loan, we need to have a constructor of the class Loan1 that accepts initial values for the loan's properties. This constructor accepts the annual interest rate for the loan, the number of years for the loan period, and the loan amount and stores them into the new Loan1 object’s annualInterestRate, numberOfYears, and loanAmount, respectively.

Note that the constructor definition starts with the access specifier (public), name of the constructor (always the same as the name of the class) and the list of parameters (to initialize the instance variables of newly created objects). Unlike methods, constructors do not have a return type.

This statement sets instance variable annualInterestRate to the first parameter value (annualInterestRate). Note that the this reference is used to distinguish the parameter of the constructor from its corresponding instance variable with the same name.

This statement sets instance variable numberOfYears to the second parameter value (numberOfYears). Note that the this reference is used to distinguish the parameter of the constructor from its corresponding instance variable with the same name.

This statement sets instance variable loanAmount to the third parameter value (loanAmount). Note that the this reference is used to distinguish the parameter of the constructor from its corresponding instance variable with the same name.

To create a loan without specifying any values for the loan properties, we need to define a constructor that receives no parameters (i.e., a default empty constructor). In this case we want to use default values for the loan properties; therefore, all we need to do is to invoke another constructor of the class that receives three parameters and pass it the default values for the loan properties (i.e., 3 % interest rate, 1-year loan period, and 1000 loan amount).

Note that Java doesn’t supply the default empty constructor when we define a constructor of our own (like in this class that has a constructor that accepts three parameters). Therefore, if we have a constructor in the class that accepts one or more parameters, we need to explicitly declare the default empty constructor to allow instantiating objects from the class without specifying any parameters.

Note that the constructor definition starts with the access specifier (public), name of the constructor (always the same as the name of the class) and the list of parameters if any (to initialize the instance variables of newly created objects). Unlike methods, constructors do not have a return type.

Also, note that when a class doesn’t have a constructor at all, Java automatically supplies a default constructor with no parameters. The default constructor is called when we instantiate an object from the class using the new keyword and empty parentheses. The default constructor auto-initializes all fields to zero-equivalent values (null for strings or object references, 0 for primitive data types, etc).

We want to create a loan with the default values for the annual interest rate, number of years for the loan period, and loan amount. We already have a constructor that accepts the value of these parameters for the loan. Therefore, all we need to do is to invoke that constructor ( using this() ) and passing that the default values for the annual interest rate, number of years for the loan period, and loan amount.
Note that we use decimal representation of percentage for the annual interest rate (0.03=3%).

This method calculates and returns the amount of monthly payments on the loan. We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as double, as it returns the amount of monthly payments that could have a decimal point.

This method does not have any parameters because the only data that we need to use in this method are the instance variables of the class and we can directly access the instance variables from the methods that are inside the class.

To calculate the amount of monthly payments on the loan, we need to know the monthly interest rate. We get the monthly interest rate of the loan by dividing the annual interest rate by the number of months in the year, i.e., 12.
The mathematical expression in this statement calculates the amount of the monthly payments on the loan.
Note that Math.pow(a, b) is a method that takes the value of the first argument a and raises it to the power of the second argument b. The returned value is a double.
